description.value: The study examined individual differences in neural responses to an emotion-word Stroop task as a function of secure-base-script knowledge, using functional magnetic resonance imaging.

spans.text: The present study addressed this need by examining individual differences in neural responses to emotional stimuli as a function of adult attachment.

value: we hypothesized that individuals lower in secure-base-script knowledge would experience unpleasant emotional stimuli as more disturbing or dysregulating and would therefore show increased activation in brain regions that regulate emotional experience

It was also expected that lower secure-base-script knowledge would elicit a greater attentional bias to such stimuli, and that this bias would require more cognitive effort and control to suppress. This effect would be instantiated in poorer performance (longer RT and more errors) and increased brain activity in regions associated with cognitive control on this task
